body: The new sentence "the 1024-character limit applies only to a value that is not whitespace only" does not describe what the code does. `tokenChangeFor` trims the value first and then `validateClaudeToken` checks `len(token) > 1024` on the trimmed token. So `"<2000 spaces>sk-ant-..."` (more than 1024 characters, not whitespace only) is accepted and verified, not refused as too long. Suggested fix: "the 1024-character limit applies to the trimmed value, so surrounding whitespace, and a whitespace-only value of any length, never makes it too long". The session works differently: there the 8192 limit applies to the raw input, and the spec states that correctly.

This alternative says that any input longer than the maximum and containing another character is refused, and it cites FR-CLT-SET-004. That holds for the LeBoncoin session, whose raw length is checked before trimming. It does not hold for the Claude token, which is trimmed before its 1024-character check. For example, 2000 spaces followed by a short token is not refused as too long; the token is verified. Suggested fix: limit the sentence to the LeBoncoin input, or say that for the Claude token the limit applies after trimming surrounding whitespace. Make the same change to the matching FR-SECRET-014 wording ("A non-empty input longer than the maximum is still rejected as before") if it is meant to cover the token.

This assertion runs after `await expect(dialog).toBeHidden()`, so `Saving settings…` (which only appears inside the open modal) can never be found; the check is vacuous. It does not prove TC-005's corner case "no progress for a verification". The frontend makes no request when both entries are untouched (TS-SECRET-019), so the stronger and simpler proof is `expect(api.puts).toEqual([])`. Alternatively, check for the progress text before the modal closes. The `/too long/` part can stay.
